sentences.text: The holotype specimen preserved the wing membrane, hair-like structures, a long tail vane, and a head crest with a bony base and large keratin extension. A head crest is an unusual feature for basal pterosaurs, which rarely show such structures in fossils.
The crest covered the posterior two-thirds of the head and was reinforced by a dozen parallel ridges.
A vertical pattern at the base of the crest was interpreted as original camouflage coloration.

The genus Pterorhynchus was named in 2002 by Stephen Czerkas and Ji Qiang. The type species of the genus is Pterorhynchus wellnhoferi. The genus name means "wing snout" and refers to the tall crest on the animal's head. The specific name wellnhoferi honors the German pterosaur researcher Peter Wellnhofer.
The holotype specimen was found in Chifeng within the Daohugou Beds.
Researchers suggested the head crest had a primarily aerodynamic function.

The fibers were described as pinnate, resembling the base of bird down feathers, and were seen as corresponding to Stage II in feather evolution. The presence of these fibers suggests that pterosaur pycnofibers and dinosaur feathers were homologous.

Czerkas and Ji originally assigned Pterorhynchus to the family Rhamphorhynchidae. Pterorhynchus belongs to the suborder Rhamphorhynchoidea. The parent group of Pterorhynchus is Rhamphorhynchinae. Pterorhynchus is classified in the family Rhamphorhynchidae.

A 2014 analysis by Andres and colleagues found Pterorhynchus to be a close relative of wukongopterids and therefore closer to pterodactyloid pterosaurs. Andres and colleagues assigned Pterorhynchus to the group Darwinoptera. Pterorhynchus is part of the unranked family Darwinoptera.

Ji assigned Pterorhynchus to the Yanliao Biota of the Haifanggou Formation during the Callovian stage. Lü Junchang in 2007 suggested the animal lived in the later Tiaojishan Formation of the same stage. Pterorhynchus lived between 165.3 and 161.5 million years ago during the Callovian.
